text:
mira: Hi -- running into a weird import error after onboarding a customer. py-sdk extras aren't installed when we use pip-tools + constraints + editable install in our CI. reverting to a regular pip install works. any ideas?

sam: Can you paste the exact commands you run and the error?

mira: repro steps:
1) python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install pip-tools==6.11.3
2) echo '.[httpx,auth]' > install-extras.txt
3) pip-compile --output-file constraints.txt pyproject.toml
4) .venv/bin/pip install -e . -c constraints.txt

Result: import of httpx.asyncClient fails: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'httpx._client' even though constraints.txt pins httpx 0.23.3 and pip reports "Requirement already satisfied" for httpx.

jordan: hmm. sounds like editable install didn't bring package extras into the env because of how -e resolves with constraints. do you see a line in pip's output that says "Installing build requirements" or a separate install for extras?

mira: pip output shows: "Processing ." then a few build steps, then "Requirement already satisfied: httpx==0.23.3 in .venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages (from -r constraints.txt (line 12))" but there's no recorded install of the SDK's extras (no redwood-sdk[httpx] wheel).

sam: two quick checks: which pip (version) and is pyproject using PEP 621 project metadata or setup.cfg/setup.py? editable-backend/pep517 behaviors differ. also pip 23+ changed some editable semantics.

mira: pip 22.3.1, build-backend is setuptools+wheel (pyproject.toml has [build-system] setuptools). We use a local editable for dev in CI.

jordan: try one of: a) pip install -e '.[httpx,auth]' -c constraints.txt (quote and bracket required in some shells) b) pip install -e .[httpx,auth] -c constraints.txt c) if using pip-tools, ensure extras are referenced in the requirements input so pip-compile includes them (e.g., add redwood-sdk[httpx,auth] to a requirements.in that you compile).

mira: tried a) and b) earlier, got "ERROR: Invalid requirement: '.[httpx,auth]'" in our Docker container shell. it may be shell/quoting weirdness in the CI executor.

sam: okay, in many CI runners the quoting gets stripped. try escaping or use double quotes. like: pip install -e "[httpx,auth]" is wrong, you want pip install -e ".[httpx,auth]". also try pip list --path . to see what the editable link produced.

mira: also discovered that when constraints.txt pins a different httpx than the project's extras specify (our extras want httpx>=0.24), pip will avoid reinstalling since constraint satisfied so you end up with httpx installed but not the SDK's extra metadata (no entry-points?). import still fails because the SDK's shim code expecting new httpx API isn't present.

jordan: right — constraints can cause a mismatch between "package installed" and "extras applied" for editable installs. workaround: ensure requirements input explicitly contains redwood-sdk[httpx,auth] so pip-compile resolves the extras and pins them, then install with -e . -c constraints.txt. alternatively, build a wheel in CI (python -m build) and pip install that wheel with -c constraints.txt instead of editable.

mira: thanks — building a wheel in CI is a good stopgap. I'll try adding redwood-sdk[httpx,auth] to requirements.in and recompile.

supportbot: For similar cases see internal KB: docs/internal/ci-editable-extras.md and RFC on constraints+editable behavior. I'll open a support ticket (SUP-12984) and tag eng-infra if this repros across runners. :white_check_mark:

mira: updated our requirements.in, compiled constraints, re-ran install — imports now succeed. leaving note: pip-tools + constraints + -e will not implicitly apply extras unless the extras are present in the compiled inputs. building wheels avoids editable semantics issues. thanks! :sparkles:
